video_title: Bob Myers on Philly Acquiring LeBron & Jaylen Brown, Building Champions,and Tough NBA Decisions

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's leadership and value to the Celtics
quotes.excerpt: You need to win a championship, guys that are of that ilk, I think, that are comfortable being uncomfortable.
quotes.quote: We needed an edge, and I think Jaylen Brown sets an edge. You need to win a championship, guys that are of that ilk, I think, that are comfortable being uncomfortable, if that makes sense. And he is one of those. And so the deal came down, and I didn't know Jaylen at all. I talked to him the day after, and I just said, listen, don't ever underestimate that you're a champion, and that there's power in that. So use that with this team. We don't have that on our team. And I said, we need you to lead. I'm going to ask you to lead.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Bryant's confidence and career goals as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: He said, I'm going to win 10 NBA championships, and then I'm going to finish my career in Italy.
quotes.quote: Kobe, my first day in that office with Arn, I went in to interview to be an intern, and Kobe was sitting in that little lounge area they had. You know this, and he was sitting on the couch, and he had a Joe Montana retro jersey, 49ers, number 16. And I literally walked in, he was the first person I saw, because you know that little lounge was right there, there was no security, there was just Kobe Bryant. And they had just lost to Utah when he missed those shots. And this dude was so confident. I said, hey, I'd like to meet you, and he started talking. And he said, I'm going to win 10 NBA championships, and then I'm going to finish my career in Italy.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Handling player frustration over role and trade requests
quotes.excerpt: The hard thing now is, do you say, or do you say we're leaving school? We're going to a new school.
quotes.quote: The hard thing now is, so one of your boys isn't playing enough as he should, two his team's not good enough, three not getting enough shots. He comes home and says, Dad, I should be, they got to run more plays for me. I'm only getting 15 shots up. The hard thing now is, do you say, or do you say we're leaving school? We're going to a new school. Because what you're talking about is, you didn't, if North Carolina didn't go well for you, you weren't just going to leave. You would walk into Coach Smith's office. Now you might have left. You might have said, I'm out of here, and left North Carolina. And nobody would have thought any problem with that. You might have played for four high schools. And so now a kid gets to the NBA, and it's hard, and he doesn't know what to do. What's he going to do? Demand a trade as a rookie? No. So now a kid that may have had to go through some hard to get to the NBA, got bailed out every time.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating player passion for basketball
quotes.excerpt: I want a tool to measure how much they love basketball. That's all I want to know.
quotes.quote: If I got to make up one thing that didn't exist, I'd say, I want a tool to measure how much they love basketball. That's all I want to know. And I put it on your forehead, and it says out of 10, Tracy's a nine, Vince's a nine. Boom. I don't care how much money they make, they're a nine. But some guys, you measure that, three.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Jermaine O'Neal's leadership impact on the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: I asked him, I said, we need some leadership. Because that's, that's not enough, there's not enough of that either.
quotes.quote: When the Warriors were in 14, Jermaine was on the team. Jermaine O'Neal who I worked with too. And Jermaine was like year 16, 17. He came back for that year, because I asked him, I said, we need some leadership. Because that's, that's not enough, there's not enough of that either, by the way, in the NBA. They ran them out. Yeah, it's, it's very hard to find leadership at any level. So I thought our team needed, and Jermaine is a very, very good leader, I think. And so he came to the team, we lost the Clippers in seven games, and he was banged up trying to play, his wrist was jacked. We lose in seven games, and I'm looking at the team going, well, Steph's looking like he could be something, Klay, Harrison Barnes, some of our young guys. Draymond played in that series. And Jermaine calls me three days after we lost, and I'm thinking he's going to tell me he's retired and whatever. He goes, hey man, listen to me, do not break this team up. And I was kind of like, what's so great about this team? We just lost in the first round. And he goes, I've been in a lot of locker rooms at the end of a season, and this team knows how to lose. He said it bothered them the right amount.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Players' obsession with making the All-Star game
quotes.excerpt: I didn't understand how much players want to make the All-Star game.
quotes.quote: I didn't understand how much players want to make the All-Star game. You guys got to be honest, because I remember talking to Igor Kokoskov one year and I go, what are we doing? We were a team was, he goes, All-Star game. We tell the All-Star game's over, and then we'll be right. And tell me about that, like, I know it's an ego thing, but forget about the money, you guys had enough money. But that was, that was the driving, that was the driving factor.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's early career frustrations and leadership
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown came to me, came to my house, and we had a sit down.

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: Jaylen Brown, right? Jaylen Brown came to me, came to my house, and we had a sit down. And he had some things that, and this was, this was many years ago before they won a championship. And you know, there was a lot of talk circling around, you know, breaking up this, this, this core with he and Jayson Tatum. So, and I was watching how they played with each other, right, year after year. And this particular year, they fell short. And it was a year where he was frustrated and was thinking about making a change, right? The media is, is talking, the fans are talking. I said, Jaylen, you got some good, bro. Like, don't, don't break this, don't break this up because I see, you know, a championship out of y'all two at some point.

text_blocks.speaker: Bob Myers
text_blocks.text: And we had him on our pod, and we was talking about this story, and I just felt like he couldn't see, you know, what, because I have no emotional attachment to any of the Boston Celtics of what they're, they're building. But he couldn't see what I was seeing. Right? And that's why I pointed that out to him and, and, you know, a year, two years later, they eventually won a championship. So, now I can, I can all to well, um, understand what Jaylen was seeing, you know, with that team.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The lack of honest conversations in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: There's not a lot of honest conversations in the NBA, I don't think.
quotes.quote: There's not a lot of honest conversations in the NBA, I don't think. Coaches are often scared to get fired, and they, especially with guys like you. They're not going to mess with guys like you. In a film session, in a practice, in a game. Man, that's why I miss Jeff Van Gundy, bro. That's why I, I hate that once he stopped coaching the Rockets, he didn't coach no more, because what you are describing is a coach that is the total opposite of that. He's one of those coaches that he's going to tell you what you don't want to hear, but what you need to hear. And he's an honest coach. So, we would come into practice one day, we don't know what's going on, we were coming into practice one day, no balls, nobody is shooting, right? Nobody is stretching. He would tell everybody to line up on the wall. Right? So we all lined up on the wall, and from one to 15, he's going to tell you to your face what he expects from you. What your role is, right? So, what that does for, for me as the leader of the team, or as the vet for the team, I know I can hold you accountable now because I know what to expect out of you, right? So, for me, Jeff, man, just to, to have that honesty amongst the team and we all know what to expect from everybody on this team, there's no surprises.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The immense power of NBA players compared to other sports
quotes.excerpt: Do you understand the power of an NBA player? As far as any other sport, the only power that is equivalent to an NBA star is an NFL quarterback.
quotes.quote: Do you understand the power of an NBA player? As far as any other sport, the only power that is equivalent to an NBA star is an NFL quarterback. And they don't act like they, when a team loses in the NFL, let's say you guys lost in a playoff game, you're up there 30 minutes after you lost. Hey, you think this team's good enough? What do you think about requesting a trade? You think you're going to stick around? They don't, the media doesn't do that to the NFL quarterback. They don't push him to say, you need to get out of here to win. Whereas with you guys, now you've got so much power, and if one of you two in the prime of your career, all you have to do is this, let's say I'm the GM. Hey, you got two minutes? Hey, look, um, I'm done here. Do you understand that could mess up the organization for five years? It happened. Yeah. Yeah. So, if I let you get that far, then I'm in trouble. I will have to have thought I did every single thing I could to stop that from happening. And then you come in and I go, listen, man, we've been, you tried, I tried. Let's figure out the best situation. But if I don't try, and I didn't wasn't ahead of you trying, and you walk in there and we don't have a relationship, and we haven't had that conversation, and I'm blindsided, then I'm in trouble.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of finding leadership in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: It's very hard to find leadership at any level.
quotes.quote: It's very hard to find leadership at any level. So I thought our team needed, and Draymond is a very, very good leader, I think. And so he came to the team, we lost the Clippers in seven games, and he was banged up trying to play, his wrist was jacked. And Draymond calls me three days after we lost, and I'm thinking he's going to tell me he's retired and whatever. He goes, hey man, listen to me, do not break this team up. And I was kind of like, what's so great about this team? We just lost in the first round. And he goes, I've been in a lot of locker rooms at the end of a season, and this team knows how to lose. He said it bothered them the right amount.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of hiring and building a championship team
quotes.excerpt: Started with ownership made a change in the executive space with Daryl and asked me to help hire somebody new.
quotes.quote: Started with ownership made a change in the executive space with Daryl and asked me to help hire somebody new. And so, that's a hard thing to do. I don't think, I wish there was like more of a pool of like obviously great executives, you know? Like you guys should be, I mean, I just want to have, I would, I mean, but it's, but Tracy, it's hard. I'm not saying you can't do it or you can't do it. It's a sacrifice. You understand? Like it is. So, when I was tasked with like, let's find some leadership, knowing what I could help, I was looking for somebody that I thought exhibited some of the things I valued. And so I interviewed a bunch of guys actually here in LA, and Ganse, the guy we ended up hiring, stood out as far as like he had had LeBron before, he had seen the rise of Cleveland. He'd been there for, I think 15 years. So he'd been around that, and they'd also been around when, when LeBron left and, and everybody stopped watching. And then the Cavs got built back up. And Kobe Altman was a big part of that, and they got good ownership, and they've done a great job there. And so watching, listening to him say, how did you manage those LeBron kind of scrutiny years and winning, and then he leaves, and then you, you kind of like buried, and then crawl, I liked his story for that. I liked that he felt like to me somebody that had a great relationship with players, with coaches. Easy to talk to.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of honesty in player-GM relationships
quotes.excerpt: I think Brad Stevens is one of the most straight shooters in the league.
quotes.quote: I think Brad Stevens is one of the most straight shooters in the league. So when you, when you work in the NBA as an executive, you usually have at least one or two, I don't want to say transactions with every other GM. So you know, if I call Tracy, I go, hey, you want to make a deal? He might be like, yeah, yeah, yeah, and then he does, I mean, that's like, I know not you're not this way. But I, you have to understand like he's honest, or he, he might tell me what I want to hear, or he might lie to me. This dude just might just lie. He lied to me two years ago, he's going to lie to me again. That's not Brad Stevens. So when Brad Stevens, um, responded with, what are you offering? Then you knew that there was a shot. Yeah. And so then it becomes 50 conversations, um, towards one, both organizations did a great job not leaking that, which is impossible. Yeah, that's what I'm about to say, that's literally impossible.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The necessity of honesty in difficult management situations
quotes.excerpt: If you wait until they walk in your house, Dad, he's 17, I'm moving out. You're screwed.
quotes.quote: What I try to do with that is, if it gets to that point, I've failed. Meaning like, you got kids. If you wait until they walk in your house, Dad, he's 17, I'm moving out. You're screwed. Because he's already, he's already made up his mind. So if I let you get that far, then I'm in trouble. I will have to have thought I did every single thing I could to stop that from happening. And then you come in and I go, listen, man, we've been, you tried, I tried. Let's figure out the best situation. But if I don't try, and I didn't wasn't ahead of you trying, and you walk in there and we don't have a relationship, and we haven't had that conversation, and I'm blindsided, then I'm in trouble.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The motivation for building a championship team
quotes.excerpt: It's hard to find competition. I think you guys know. Yes. And I didn't play in the NBA.
quotes.quote: It's hard to find competition. I think you guys know. Yes. And I didn't play in the NBA, but I, and that's why I didn't love the agency thing because I wasn't competing. Um, I love getting to know you, I love getting to know players, um, I love being around, I never thought I'd be around the NBA that close. But then when I realized there might be another opportunity to compete for someone like me, you either have a choice to coach or be an executive. If you can't play. And I don't have enough money to own. And so you, that's your choice. So for me, stepping away, there's two things I missed. The, um, I don't want to, I don't want to say this right, the locker room, like the people, like the, the people. Like you guys, I bet you miss that. Absolutely. The camaraderie. The camaraderie. Absolutely. Like fighting for a cause. Like we're all pulling in the same direction. No jobs can mimic that, in my opinion. No, there's no industry where you're all trying to win this trophy that only one team gets, and you're all killing yourself to get it. That doesn't exist. You win or you lose 82 times a year, and the playoffs, and I missed that fight and that competitiveness, and so trying to figure out how to feel that again was, was probably the motivation.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of building a championship team
quotes.excerpt: I mean, he chose the one that was, there's only one reason, it's to win.
quotes.quote: I mean, he chose the one that was, there's only one reason, it's to win. It wasn't because I played there before, I grew up there, I want to play with my friend. It was because I want to win. So I'm going to go where I want to go that gives me the best chance to win. Does that make sense? 100%. Yeah, but is that the hardest, the hardest, the hardest road is staying where you was. That's the hardest. Okay, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, that is the hard. And I don't know, that's you'd have to have him on, ask him that. But I, I'm not going to knock him just because he goes from team to team and tries to win a championship. And there's a different, totally different era. I guess what I was saying is, what would have been easier to go back somewhere, to go to play in Miami or Cleveland? Or do you guys think no?

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of roster construction and team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: We also look at the center in Joel Embiid that hasn't been healthy for the last couple years.
quotes.quote: Yes, we look at this team as the best chance for them to win, but we also look at the center in Joel Embiid that hasn't been healthy for the last couple years. But, but, but let's, let's, but there. But structure. Totally. By the way, if Joel was, if he had no issue, then it's done, done. Like forget it. There's nothing to talk about. So yeah, sure, I'm sure there was a pause of like, okay, is he going to be healthy? Now if you see him working out like lately, he's, he's, he's got the message. He's doing it.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Bob Myers on the emotional difficulty of moving on from core players
quotes.excerpt: If I had to move off of Klay, I might have had a hard time with that.
quotes.quote: Had I stayed in Golden State, it might have. Like if I had to move off of Klay, I might have had a hard time with that. If I had been there and I had to do something with Draymond or Steph or something like that, that would have been personal because of what we went through together. Guys like Iguodala, Livingston, guys that won multiple championships. If I don't feel that, then what the hell was I doing? If I don't have a relationship with those guys, now there's not 10 of them, but there's a few guys where I would have a hard time. I think I'd still do the right thing for the organization, but it would be really hard to tell a guy that, all that that guy did for my life. My life, personally, forget about the organizations, which is what you're hired to do, what's best for the organization when you're an executive. But when you win multiple championships with people that played and gave everything and changed my life personally, not the organizations, mine, how can I not let that affect me?

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Bob Myers on prioritizing the human element in executive decision making
quotes.excerpt: I would always try to see whatever was good in the player and focus on that.
quotes.quote: I was never a guy, because I would always try to see whatever was good in the player and focus on that. And understand like, people don't totally know what it's like to be you guys. Your life is, as much as people want to be an NBA player, it's not a perfect life. Getting to know you, I know the stuff you've been through. So as a person, I always made it feel like, I'm going to at least, if you walk in and you go, hey, I don't want to be here, I would want to try to make, especially if you had given the best you could, to put you in a situation.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Handling trade rumors and player communication
quotes.excerpt: You walk in my office and you go, you go, uh, you can trade me? What should I say?
quotes.quote: Okay, let's say you walk in my office and you go, you go, uh, you can trade me? What should I say? I did this happened. I'll tell you what happened with the player. But what, what do you think I should do? Player comes in and asks you that question. You say to me, hoops hype, social media, blah, wherever I'm working, they're trying to trade Vince Carter. They're trying to trade, he's, you're in trade rumors to the point where like everybody knows you're in a trade rumor. Now you haven't been traded, nobody's saying anything to the organization. You walk in one day and you go, F this, I'm going to find out what the hell's going on around here. Right? Because you're sick of it. Right? Because you're a human being. Right? You're tired of it. Right? So you come in and you go, hey, you got a minute? Yeah, what's up? You can trade me? What should I say? And I did, I'll tell you what I said, but what should I say?

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of honesty in player-GM communication
quotes.excerpt: I could lie. But I'm not going to lie, not because I'm not going to lie to you, but because I got to go to bed at night knowing I didn't lie.
quotes.quote: I could lie. But I'm not going to lie, not because I'm not going to lie to you, but because I got to go to bed at night knowing I didn't lie. I didn't, I'm not going to lie. I got a challenge, I want to, I want to dive deeper into your decision making and, and how you get there for, because I, I know me being young and you being part of that, that managing, uh, management group for me as a young player, when I look at, you know, agents, I sometimes wonder, are they really like watching games and understanding what's being going on, you know, in the game? Not with the team, but actually on the court.

quotes.speaker: Bob Myers
quotes.summary_phrase: Bob Myers on the importance of building relationships and winning
quotes.excerpt: He contributed to winning. Yeah, but I want to know that like we went through something together.

text_blocks.speaker: Bob Myers
text_blocks.text: He was a decent guy. He was a good guy. Not some genius GM, not some he's the architect. He's a good dude when we see each other.

text_blocks.speaker: Bob Myers
text_blocks.text: Yeah, but I want to know that like we went through something together and we got to know each other and we did something together. And we did it the right way.

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: Yeah, you did it the right way.

text_blocks.speaker: Bob Myers
text_blocks.text: We did the right way. And that's it, because what else, I mean, I don't know what, sure you ask a lot of people that. I don't know what, I mean, what on your tombstone is it going to say? People are going to give a shit if you got six rings or two or what does it fucking matter?

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: You can have that on there.

text_blocks.speaker: Bob Myers
text_blocks.text: No, but it gets knocked over and then who gives, nobody cares. So yeah, I think just just going through it, you know, building those relationships and doing it the right way.
